{{Short description|Physics models of a 1D gas of bosons}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2024}}In [[physics]], the '''Lieb–Liniger model''' describes a gas of particles moving in one dimension and satisfying [[Bose–Einstein statistics]]. More specifically, it describes a one dimensional [[Bose gas]] with [[Dirac delta function|Dirac delta]] interactions. It is named after [[Elliott H. Lieb]] and {{ill|Werner Liniger|de}} who introduced the model in 1963.<ref name="ll63">Elliott H. Lieb and Werner Liniger, ''Exact Analysis of an Interacting Bose Gas. I. The General Solution and the Ground State'', Physical Review 130: 1605–1616, 1963</ref> The model was developed to compare and test [[Nikolay Bogolyubov]]'s theory of a [[weakly interacting Bose gas]].<ref name=":0" /> It can be seen as one model in the theory of [[generalized hydrodynamics]].

==Definition==
Given <math>N</math> [[Boson|bosons]] moving in one-dimension on the <math> x </math>-axis defined from <math>[0,L]</math> with [[periodic boundary conditions]], a state of the ''N''-body system must be described by a many-body [[wave function]] <math>\psi(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_j, \dots,x_N)</math>. The [[Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)|Hamiltonian]], of this model is introduced as

: <math>   H = -\sum_{i=1}^N \frac{\partial^2}{\partial x_i^2} + 2c \sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{j>i}^N \delta(x_i-x_j)\ , </math>

where <math>\delta </math> is the [[Dirac delta function]]. The constant <math>c</math> denotes the strength of the interaction, <math>c>0</math> represents a repulsive interaction and <math>c<0</math> an attractive interaction.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |last=Eckle |first=Hans-Peter |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=g0KjDwAAQBAJ&dq=lieb+liniger+model&pg=PA549 |title=Models of Quantum Matter: A First Course on Integrability and the Bethe Ansatz |date=2019-07-29 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-166804-3 |language=en}}</ref> The hard core limit <math>c\to\infty</math> is known as the [[Tonks–Girardeau gas]].<ref name=":1" />

For a collection of bosons, the wave function is unchanged under permutation of any two particles (permutation symmetry), i.e., <math>\psi(\dots, x_i,\dots, x_j, \dots) = \psi(\dots, x_j,\dots, x_i, \dots) </math> for all <math>i \neq j</math> and <math>\psi</math> satisfies <math>\psi( \dots, x_j=0, \dots ) =\psi(\dots, x_j=L,\dots )</math> for all <math>j</math>.

The delta function in the Hamiltonian gives rise to a boundary condition when two coordinates, say <math>x_1 </math> and <math>x_2</math> are equal. The condition is that as <math>x_2</math> approaches  <math>x_1</math> from above (<math>x_2 \searrow x_1</math>), the derivative satisfies 
:<math>\left.\left(\frac{\partial}{\partial x_2} - \frac{\partial}{\partial x_1} \right) \psi (x_1, x_2)\right|_{x_2=x_1+}= c \psi (x_1=x_2)</math>.

== Solution ==
[[File:lieb-liniger-1.gif|thumb|450px| Fig. 1: The ground state energy (per particle) <math>e</math> as a function of the interaction strength per density <math>\gamma=Lc/N</math>, from.<ref name="ll63" />  ]]The time-independent [[Schrödinger equation]] <math>H\psi = E\psi</math>, is solved by explicit construction of <math>\psi</math>. Since <math>\psi </math> is symmetric it is completely determined by its values in the simplex <math>\mathcal{R} </math>, defined by the condition that <math>0 \leq x_1 \leq x_2 \leq \dots, \leq x_N \leq L</math>.

The solution can be written in the form of a [[Bethe ansatz]] as<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Lieb |first=Elliott |date=2008 |title=Lieb-Liniger model of a Bose Gas |journal=Scholarpedia |language=en |volume=3 |issue=12 |pages=8712 |doi=10.4249/scholarpedia.8712 |doi-access=free |issn=1941-6016}}</ref>

: <math> \psi(x_1, \dots, x_N) =  \sum_P a(P)\exp \left( i \sum_{j=1}^N k_{P j} x_j\right)  </math>,

with wave vectors <math>0 \leq k_1 \leq k_2 \leq \dots, \leq k_N </math>, where the sum is over all <math>N !</math> permutations, <math>P</math>, of the integers <math>1,2, \dots, N</math>, and <math>P</math> maps <math>1,2,\dots,N</math> to <math> P_1,P_2,\dots,P_N</math>. The coefficients <math>a(P)</math>, as well as the <math>k</math>'s are determined by the condition <math>H\psi =E\psi</math>, and this leads to a total energy
: <math> E= \sum_{j=1}^N\, k_j^2 </math>,
with the amplitudes given by
: <math>  a(P) = \prod_{1\leq i<j \leq N} \left(1+\frac{ic}{k_{Pi}  -k_{Pj}}\right) \, . </math><ref>{{cite journal |first=Teunis C. |last=Dorlas |title=Orthogonality and Completeness of the Bethe Ansatz Eigenstates of the nonlinear Schrödinger model |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |volume=154 |issue=2 |pages=347–376 |year=1993 |doi=10.1007/BF02097001 |bibcode = 1993CMaPh.154..347D |s2cid=122730941 |url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104252974 }}</ref>

These equations determine <math>\psi</math> in terms of the <math>k</math>'s. These lead to <math>N</math> equations:<ref name=":0" />

: <math> L\,  k_j= 2\pi I_j\  -2 \sum_{i=1}^N  \arctan \left(\frac{k_j-k_i}{c} \right)    \qquad \qquad \text{for } j=1, \, \dots,\, N \   ,  </math>

where <math>I_1 < I_2 < \cdots < I_N</math> are integers when <math>N</math> is odd and, when <math>N</math> is even, they take values <math>\pm \frac12, \pm \frac32, \dots</math> . For the ground state the <math>I</math>'s satisfy
: <math> I_{j+1} - I_j = 1, \quad {\rm for} \ 1\leq  j <N \qquad
\text{and } I_1=-I_N. </math>
